optionReasons.clf-ini-001:option:0: The cloud REDUZ the supply time (minutes) — does not increase.
optionReasons.clf-ini-001:option:1: Cloud eliminates long-term hardware contracts — paid for use.
optionReasons.clf-ini-001:option:3: Buying servers in advance is exactly the on-premises model that the cloud replaces.

finalJustifications: Because the cloud swaps the initial investment in hardware (CapEx) for variable expense according to use (OpEx) — you only pay what you consume.
Because in the cloud the hardware is acquired in fixed monthly installments, diluting the capital investment throughout the contract of use.
Because CapEx comes to mean cost per execution: each workload pays a single capital fee when it is provided in the cloud.
Because the AWS assumes the client's capital expenses by purchasing the on-premises legacy hardware and reselling as cloud credits.

optionReasons.clf-ini-002:option:0: Automatic encryption is a security feature — does not define elasticity.
optionReasons.clf-ini-002:option:2: Financial reports are billing tools — nothing to do with scale.
optionReasons.clf-ini-002:option:3: Migration of data between regions is portability — elasticity is about AJUSTAR resources on demand.

finalJustifications: Because elasticity is to scale resources up and down automatically according to demand — without waste or unavailability.
Because elasticity means that the servers never become unavailable: the AWS resets the load between data centers before failure.
Because elasticity is the ability to migrate resources between regions without additional cost, taking advantage of the lowest price of each locality.
Because elasticity guarantees a fixed monthly price independent of use, absorbing peaks of demand without variation in the invoice.

optionReasons.clf-ini-003:option:0: A single isolated data center describes another AZ (or part of it) — the REGION is the set of VARIOUS AZs.
optionReasons.clf-ini-003:option:1: Type of instance EC2 is something else (t3.micro etc.) — is not a geographical concept.
optionReasons.clf-ini-003:option:3: CDN is the CloudFront — the Region is geographical infrastructure.

finalJustifications: Because a Region is a geographical area with multiple Availability Zones isolated from each other — the basis of high availability.
Because a region is the main data center that the AWS keeps in each country, from where local services are distributed to customers.
Because each region contains exactly one dedicated Availability Zone, and redundancy is done replicating between neighboring regions.
Because regions share the same network and energy infrastructure, which reduces cost and synchronizes services globally.

optionReasons.clf-ini-014:option:0: Performance Efficiency strives to use resources efficiently — Automatic fault recovery is the Reliability Pillar.
optionReasons.clf-ini-014:option:2: Security pillar deals with data protection and identities — not fault recovery.
optionReasons.clf-ini-014:option:3: Cost optimization seeks to eliminate unnecessary expenditure — not resilience.

finalJustifications: Because the Reliability pillar focuses on the load perform correctly and if RECUPERAR automated faults.
Because Reliability guarantees the lowest cost per instance when dimensioning capacity exactly according to the system demand.
Because Reliability eliminates the need for backups: automatic recovery makes data copies redundant.
Because Reliability is the only mandatory pillar of the framework — the rest are optional architectural recommendations.
